newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila Central Bank leaves overnight rate flat.
newsitem.headline: Manila Central Bank leaves overnight rate flat.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank decided on Tuesday to leave its overnight money market rates unchanged, the Bank's Treasurer Sergio Edeza said.
There had been market speculation of a rise following Monday's increase in Treasury bill rates.
The Central Bank's overnight borrowing rate currently stands at 10.0 percent and the overnight lending rate at 12.65 percent.
Late last week, the Central Bank lifted its overnight borrowing rate from 9.9 percent, a move which dealers said was aimed at attracting inflows and siphoning off more liquidity.
That led the benchmark 91-day Treasury bill rate to jump to 10.107 percent on Monday from 9.583 percent last week.
Inflows had slackened after the 91-day T-bill rate fell to single-digit levels in recent weeks due to low inflation and heightened liquidity in the system.
Government officials also said the Central Bank's action was intended to stop peso speculation ahead of another expected hike in U.S. interest rates in May.
